packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: no proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. The overview shows a library stamp and a pencil shelfmark "Fragm. lat. 13" at the foot; noted as visible only, not used. The text itself names its subject in its closing line (see image-004 l11); I report that as a reading, not as an identification of the work or author. I did nothing beyond the stated rules (I listed the packet directory only to get image filenames and compared PROMPT.md files across packets).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- One face of a single leaf (paper or thin parchment, it looks like paper with chain-line shadows / or offset of text from another leaf visible as vertical bands of mirror-image writing showing through). Overview image-001; four horizontal native-resolution strips image-002 (top) to image-005 (bottom), overlapping by 1-2 lines.
- Single block of long lines, not columns. Late medieval cursive / bastarda-type hand, brown ink. No red apart from a faint reddish stain at the right edge.
- Line-initial capitals set off at the left (enlarged ink "A" with dotted decoration in line 1). Virgules (/) inside lines mark internal pauses, and the lines rhyme internally (e.g. "accedit / recedit / decedit"; "datur / ... ") - so this looks like rhymed verse/prose (rhythmic verses), written as long lines. Interpretation.
- Interlinear additions over lines 2, 3, 4 and 12 (glosses or alternative readings: e.g. "fulserat", "agnes").
- Top margin: scribbles/pen trials (e.g. "[ ] q(ui)tac(?) & s(an)c(t)a(?)", "deus(?) ..."), and a pen-trial line above line 1. Bottom: a pen-trial flourish.
- After a gap, a block of 5 lines in the same hand appears to be an author signature riddle ("Nomen auctoris ... queris") and two lines on "dyptong-" - a separate closing section.

SPANS SELECTED: the whole text (21 lines + interlinear). Line numbers from top of each tile; overlap: image-003 l1 = image-002 l6; image-004 l1-2 = image-003 l9-10; image-005 l1 = image-004 l12 (partial).

TRANSCRIPTION

image-002 l3: Tenera (con)iuncula(?) vite trivit(?) tenella p(er) t(er)ma(?) dena spacia

image-005 l3: [ ] tibi sit p(r)imum. tri(?). medium. ine(?). porro p(r)imum(?)

image-005 (below): pen-trial flourish; pencil shelfmark and oval stamp (modern).

LIMITATIONS
- Cursive hand with heavy abbreviation; many word forms are uncertain, especially in lines 1-3 and 12-16. Expansions in parentheses are mine; (?) marks doubt.
- Interlinear words are placed over the line they sit above; whether they are glosses or corrections is not clear.
- Mirror-image offset of another text shows through in vertical bands and interferes with a few letters (centre and left of lines 6-16).
- No second face supplied; I cannot say what is on the other side.
